title: A D2C supplements brand with strong first-order ROAS but broken LTV — fixed with subscriptions and a WhatsApp refill loop
content:
A Bengaluru D2C supplements brand spent ₹14L/month on Meta and Google. First-order ROAS looked healthy at 3.1x, blended CAC was ₹640, AOV ₹1,180. But 90-day repeat sat at 19% and 12-month LTV had stalled at ₹1,450, so true CAC payback stretched past 5 months — the brand was profitable on paper, broke in cash. The founder wanted to add ₹6L of fresh top-of-funnel. We froze that and bought the second order instead.

We launched 'Subscribe & Save 15%' on the two consumable hero SKUs (whey, daily greens), and a WhatsApp refill loop on AiSensy: an order-day +25 reminder, one-tap reorder, and a day +45 winback for lapsed buyers — backstopped by a 4-email lifecycle for the rest. Subscriptions were seeded at checkout and in the post-purchase WhatsApp.

Over 4 months, 27% of repeat buyers moved to subscription, 90-day repeat rose from 19% to 34%, and 12-month LTV climbed to ₹2,380 (+64%). WhatsApp drove 41% of all reorders at near-zero marginal cost, lifting LTV:CAC from 2.3x to 3.7x on flat ad spend.
lesson: When first-order ROAS is strong but LTV is flat, the leak is retention, not reach. Buy the second and third order with a subscription plan plus a near-zero-cost WhatsApp refill loop before you spend a rupee more on first orders.
